tests.title: Visitor searches unique keyword, selects Repositories filter, opens public acme-docs while private secret-research stays hidden; clearing query drops results and direct private access is denied
checks: Global search box has accessible name Search; typing the keyword and pressing Enter shows repository results directly
Result for acme-docs has a link with accessible name exactly acme-docs and displays alice-dev/acme-docs, description, Public visibility, and update time
No result for secret-research is shown to the visitor
Clicking the acme-docs result opens an overview heading containing alice-dev/acme-docs
Clearing the query or switching to a non-matching filter removes old results; directly reopening secret-research still requires authentication or denies access after refresh

tests.title: Signed-in user searches for acme-docs and opens it; session-authenticated repository overview persists after refresh or reopening
checks: After sign-in, the account menu shows alice-dev and protected pages are accessible
Searching acme-docs from any page and pressing Enter yields the repository result whose link name is exactly acme-docs
Clicking the result opens the alice-dev/acme-docs overview heading
Refreshing or reopening the visible destination preserves the repository overview and authenticated state
A rejected or empty search leaves the original page state unchanged

tests.title: Searching a nonexistent repository query displays No results and stays empty after returning home and repeating the same query
checks: Entering a query with no matching repository displays No results
No repository result link or metadata is rendered for the absent query
Returning to the home page and repeating the same query still displays No results
Reloading the results page does not restore stale matches or old result links

tests.title: Searching the exact private repository name secret-research exposes no result link to an unauthorized visitor and direct access remains denied
checks: Searching secret-research does not display a result link for the private repository
No unauthorized private-repository metadata appears in results
Directly opening secret-research redirects to sign-in or displays access denied
After refresh or reopening, the private repository content is not shown to the visitor

tests.title: Signed-in user creates a private repository with README and description in personal namespace; overview, README, initialization commit, and repository list persist after reload
checks: New repository form shows labeled Owner, Repository name, Description, Public/Private radios, Add a README file checkbox, and Create repository button
Submitting a unique name with Private, README checked, and the described description opens the owner/repository overview
Overview heading contains the new repository name, Private marker, descriptive text, and README file link
Default branch contains README and commit history contains one initialization commit
Repository appears in the target owner's repository list; after refresh owner, visibility, README, and initialization commit remain

tests.title: Duplicate and empty repository names in the default personal namespace are rejected; creation form stays open and no repository is created
checks: Submitting a duplicate repository name in the default personal namespace keeps the form open and does not open the existing repository heading
An empty repository name is rejected without requiring further input
The form remains on the creation page and retains non-sensitive input after the rejected submit
After refresh or reopening, no new repository appears and the existing repository state is unchanged

tests.title: Repository creation in an unauthorized organization namespace or any persistence failure is rejected atomically with no partial repository, branch, README, or commit
checks: Selecting an organization namespace where the user lacks repository-creation permission displays the applicable reason and blocks creation
No repository record is created for the failed submission
No default branch, README file, or initialization commit is created as a partial result
After reload, failed input and existing repository states remain unchanged and no partial repository is visible

tests.title: User forks readable public acme-docs into a target namespace as an independent repository; overview shows Forked from acme-docs and copied history, and fork/source relationship persists after reload
checks: Source overview displays Fork button; fork form contains Repository name field, Create fork button, and defaults to the signed-in user's personal namespace
Creating the fork opens the target owner/fork-name heading with visible Forked from acme-docs text and a source repository link
Default branch of the fork contains the accessible files and history copied from the source; source repository remains unchanged
Fork appears in the target owner's repository list; refreshing the fork page and repository list preserves the fork and source link

tests.title: Fork with conflicting existing name acme-docs-fork, missing target permission, or inaccessible source is rejected and no fork is created
checks: Using the existing fork name acme-docs-fork in the target personal namespace shows a conflict and does not create a fork
A user without creation permission in the target namespace cannot create the fork
An inaccessible private source repository cannot be forked by an unauthorized user
After reload, no new fork record exists and the source repository, branches, and history are unchanged

tests.title: Visitor copies HTTPS or SSH clone value from Code popover on a public repository; page shows Copied, keeps repository heading, and leaves repository read-only state unchanged
checks: Code button opens clone popover with HTTPS and SSH tabs and a Copy clone value button
Copying the selected protocol writes the complete clone value to the clipboard and displays Copied feedback
Repository heading remains visible and files, commit history, and visibility are unchanged
After closing and reopening the popover, the selected protocol remains visible and the repository heading persists; a user without private-repository access cannot obtain the clone value

tests.title: Signed-in user with view permission copies a clone value from a private repository and the read-only session state persists after refresh or reopening
checks: After sign-in with view permission, Code button on the private repository opens the clone popover
HTTPS or SSH clone value identifies the current repository and can be copied with Copied feedback
Copying does not modify repository files, commit history, or visibility
After refresh or reopening, the authenticated session and repository page remain accessible and unchanged; unauthorized users are not shown the clone popover

tests.title: Visitor opens public acme-docs overview and sees owner/repository heading, Public marker, description, default branch, file list, and Code/Issues/Pull requests entries; reload preserves state and private address is denied
checks: Opening the public repository address displays a heading containing alice-dev/acme-docs and a visible Public marker
Description, default branch, and file list are displayed on the overview
Code, Issues, and Pull requests navigation entries are available
Clicking a file name opens the file-content page; refreshing or reopening the same address preserves the repository heading and state
Opening secret-research without authorization does not show its content and access is denied

tests.title: Admin changes a private repository to Public via Settings, General, Danger Zone and Confirm visibility; Public marker appears, visitor can open the address, and visibility persists after reload
checks: Admin sees Change visibility button in Danger Zone and the confirmation flow provides Public radio and Confirm visibility
After confirming Public, repository overview displays the Public marker
Unauthenticated visitor refreshing or opening the same address sees the repository heading and can view public content; search and lists also show it
After refreshing the settings page and overview, visibility remains Public and the updated access rules stay in effect

tests.title: Non-Admin collaborator does not see Change visibility and cannot change visibility; private repository remains Private with unchanged state after reload
checks: Non-Admin signed-in user may have Settings or Branches available but no Change visibility button is rendered
Any attempted visibility-change request is rejected if submitted
Private marker and private access rules remain unchanged after the attempt and after reload
The absence of the Admin visibility control is not merely a disabled control; the operation is unavailable
